description: A mountain valley worn by rain, as a terrain for a game engine. The ground is a heightfield of 257 × 257 samples over size × size metres: a valley winding along X, its floor falling from the high end (+X) to the low end (-X) between walls of ridged mountains on both sides, from 0 at the lowest point of the river bed to height at the highest ridge. Rain wears it in three steps, all scaled by erosion (0 leaves the ground raw): gullies are cut down the walls where the water gathers (heightfield_flow), sediment fans are laid on the floor where they reach it, and droplet erosion (heightfield_erode) wears the whole ground and settles what it carries. The river follows the valley's centre line on a bed that falls all the way, river_depth below the floor, in a channel of varying width (the river curve's point attribute width, in metres) cut into the floor with sloping banks. Layers: flow (0..1, the water draining through each sample, on a log scale), sediment (metres of fans and settled material) and river (1 under the water, fading up the banks). The river output is that bed as a curve; the preview is the ground as a mesh with a colour map painted from the layers: grass (fresher where water gathers), rock on the slopes, darker gullies, pale fans on the floor, wet gravel on the banks and dark water in the channel. Asserts check that the ground stays between 0 and height and that the river never rises along its course.

height.label: height
height.desc: from the valley floor to the highest ridge (m)

erosion.label: erosion
erosion.desc: how long the rain wears the ground; 0 leaves it raw

river_depth.label: river depth
river_depth.desc: how deep the river cuts into the valley floor (m)

seed.label: seed
seed.desc: changes the mountains, not the look

walls.note: the bends come from a golden angle per seed, not rand(): rand() in a heightfield_layer expression costs about a microsecond a call (F-124)

params.expression:
// the valley: walls rising from a floor that falls from +X to -X
0.55 * pow(mask, 1.2) + 0.04 * (x / size + 0.5)

// cut them in
value - erosion * 0.12 * mask

// lay the fans: up to 5 cells of sediment, the more rain, the thicker
value + erosion * 5 * cell * fan

params.code:
// the channel's half width, for the sweep
@pscale = @width;

carved.note: the channel stamped flat at the bed, its banks blended over radius; mask river: 1 under the water, fading up the banks

params.expression:
// the channel and its banks, a little wider
river

banks.note: heightfield_project blends its radius from the cells a polygon stamp covers, which leaves cell-sized steps along the banks; this blur smooths them, and the bed mid-channel stays as stamped

params.expression:
// sediment (m): the fans, and what the rain carried and settled
sediment + debris + erosion * 5 * cell * fan

no_debris.note: one node per layer: heightfield_layer delete takes a single layer name, and a list silently deletes nothing (F-119)

params.expression:
// pale fans where the gullies reach the floor (the fan layer of input 1), palest where they are thickest
0.95 * smoothstep(0.03, 0.7, b_fan) * (1 - rock)

// the river, softened: highest mid-channel
river

red.note: the colours are painted as layers and written with heightfield_to_tex: bake_vertex_color with a paint wrangle took about 550 ms (F-124)

colour_map.note: heightfield_to_tex puts the -Z row at the top of the image while heightfield_to_mesh gives -Z the uv v = 0 (the bottom), so the map is mirrored in v here to land on its own samples (F-122): remove this node when F-122 lands and name colour_pack valley_colour

terrain.label: Terrain
terrain.description: The eroded ground from 0 to height, 257 × 257 samples, with the layers flow, sediment and river.

river.label: River
river.description: The river's course along the valley floor, on its bed, falling all the way from the high end to the low end, with its width in metres on every point.

preview.label: Preview
preview.description: The terrain as a mesh with a colour map painted from its layers: rock on the slopes, grass on the floor, darker gullies, pale sediment fans, gravel banks and water in the river channel.
